claims.text: AMS affects 25 percent of visitors sleeping above 2,450 m (8,000 ft) in Colorado
claims.quote: 25% of all visitors sleeping at altitudes >2,450 m (>8,000 ft) in Colorado

claims.text: Unacclimatized travelers to a sleeping altitude of 2,450 m or higher are at risk
claims.quote: Any unacclimatized traveler proceeding to a sleeping altitude of ≥2,450 m (≥8,000 ft)

claims.text: AMS onset usually 2 to 12 hours after arrival
claims.quote: Symptom onset is usually 2–12 hours after initial arrival at a high altitude

claims.text: Headache cardinal symptom with anorexia, dizziness, fatigue or nausea
claims.quote: headache is the cardinal symptom, usually accompanied by ≥1 of the following: anorexia, dizziness, fatigue, nausea

claims.text: AMS improves with descent of 300 m (1,000 ft) or more; acetaminophen or ibuprofen for headache
claims.quote: AMS improves rapidly with a descent of 300 m (1,000 ft) or more ... ibuprofen 600 mg or acetaminophen 500 mg every 8 hours

claims.text: Acetazolamide prevention 125 mg every 12 hours starting the day before ascent; treatment dose studied 250 mg as 2 doses 8 hours apart
claims.quote: 125 mg every 12 hours, beginning the day before ascent ... To date, the only dose studied for treatment is 250 mg (2 doses taken 8 hours apart)

claims.text: HACE signs; rare below 4,300 m; in remote areas start descent; dexamethasone 8 mg once then 4 mg every 6 hours
claims.quote: altered mental status, ataxia, confusion, and drowsiness ... HACE is rare, especially at elevations <4,300 m (<14,000 ft) ... initiate descent for anyone suspected of having HACE ... HACE: 8 mg once, then 4 mg every 6 hours

claims.text: HAPE early signs; descent urgent and mandatory; mild HAPE can be treated with oxygen over 2-4 days and bedrest
claims.quote: chest congestion, cough, exaggerated dyspnea on exertion ... In most circumstances, descent is urgent and mandatory. ... can be treated with oxygen over 2–4 days and bedrest at the current altitude

claims.text: Nifedipine 30 mg sustained-release every 12 hours or 20 mg every 8 hours for HAPE prevention or treatment
claims.quote: The adult dose for prevention or treatment is 30 mg of the sustained-release version every 12 hours or 20 mg every 8 hours.

claims.text: People allergic to sulfa antibiotics can take acetazolamide; caution with anaphylaxis or multiple drug allergies
claims.quote: Thus, people allergic to sulfa antibiotics can take acetazolamide.
